I'm a historian by education and profession. One of the first things you learn is that there is no such thing as an unbiased history. This is why you must read widely and broadly. Many people think the term "history" means "the past." It's not. History is what is written about the past; therefore, history is always going to be filtered by the experiences and inclinations of the people who write it. Even people who lived through historical events, what we call primary sources, are not always reliable. There is a thing called "latent history" which accounts for the bias that comes from the people who experience historical events. When we experience something historic, we don't always full appreciate the significance of it. Sometimes we cannot see things clearly because we cannot assess the historical magnitude of events. The interpretation can be flawed because of the limited perspective in what is then the present. Only with time and separation can a fair assessment be made.

If you want to read history, read a lot of it by a lot of different historians. Realize that they all have bias and seek to understand the truth that is hidden behind the bias. The most important attribute for reading history is empathy.
